the transition of M. crystallinumn from C3 photosynthetic to CAM metabolism involves a change of the subunit composition and the specific activity of the tonoplasmtic ATPase and a de-novo synthesis and accumulation of tonoplast proteins.
the tonoplast of CAM plants contains a higher amount of ATPase, which is probably the major enzyme involved in the energization of the tonoplast.
the tonoplast ATP-ase is responsible for energization of malic acid accumulation in CAM and that this enzyme is synthesized de-novo in the course of CAM induction.

the question of how the induction of CAM is related to changes in the tonoplast.

the question of how the induction of CAM is related to changes in the protein composition of the tonoplasmic membrane.

the tonoplast ATP-ase is the main enzyme responsible to energize malate accumulation during the induction of CAM and that the tonoplast pyrophosphate is of minor importance.
the induction of CAM is not only accompanied by de-nova synthesis of new polypeptides but that the CAM state also induces changes in the composition of existing polypeptides.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transition from C3 photosynthetic to CAM metabolism is accompanied by changes in the tonoplast proteins, in the tonoplast ATP hydrolytic capacity, and in the subunit composition and regulation of the tonoplast proton pumps.
the tonoplast of M. crystallinurn is characterized by a large number of proteins, which are synthesized de novo in response to the change of the photosynthetic metabolism from C3 to CAM.
CAM is accompanied by a de-novo synthesis and/or an increase of the amount of tonoplast proteins, especially the ATPase.
